understanding.vision:
HashSlip fingerprints exact piped bytes and prints a JSON receipt with byte count, SHA-256 and optional label.

Full brief: PRODUCT-BRIEF.md
understanding.users: People fingerprinting data in shell pipelines without temporary input files.
understanding.first_user_moment: Pipe bytes to python /absolute/path/hashslip.py and receive one newline-terminated JSON receipt.
understanding.scope_in: One root hashslip.py using only Python standard library; raw stdin through EOF; exact bytes/sha256/label JSON fields; exact optional --label TEXT; help and usage errors; absolute-path invocation from another cwd; no runtime files/network/install.
understanding.scope_out: GUI, file-input flags, algorithms other than SHA-256, dependencies, installation, network requests, input normalization or decoding.
understanding.quality_bar: Preserve raw bytes including NUL/FF/invalid UTF-8, distinguish trailing newlines, count UTF-8 bytes, preserve label text. Success exit 0 and empty stderr; errors exit 2 and empty stdout; help exits promptly without consuming stdin.
understanding.done_feels_like: The script works from another directory, the brief's empty/ASCII/newline/UTF-8/binary/label/help/error cases are checked through the real CLI, and handover gives its absolute path, useful invocation and honest validation limits.

HashSlip fingerprints exact piped bytes and prints a JSON receipt with byte count, SHA-256 and optional label.

Full brief: PRODUCT-BRIEF.md

nodes.title: Exact pipeline receipts
nodes.text: Fingerprint raw piped bytes with optional label and usable CLI diagnostics.

nodes.title: Exact raw-byte receipt
nodes.text: Read raw stdin through EOF without decoding, trimming or normalization; emit exactly bytes integer, sha256 lowercase 64-character digest, label null by default, one JSON object plus newline. Success exit 0, stderr empty. S1-S5 independently catch empty-input errors, text/newline normalization, character counting and invalid-UTF8 rejection; no existing scenario covers each distinct input behavior.

nodes.title: Exact optional metadata
nodes.text: --label TEXT preserves spaces and non-ASCII exactly and changes no input hash or byte count. S6 compares the same hello receipt with exact label; unlabeled scenarios cannot detect label mutation or hashing label metadata.

nodes.title: Prompt help and usage errors
nodes.text: --help exits 0, explains stdin, JSON and --label without reading stdin first. Missing label, unknown flag, and unexpected positional each exit 2 with no stdout and useful stderr. S7-S10 hold stdin open to catch parsers that read before processing arguments; successful receipt cases do not exercise rejection or prompt exit.

nodes.title: Standalone standard-library script
nodes.text: Deliver only root hashslip.py, callable by absolute path from another cwd, no installation, third-party packages, runtime files or network. S6 executes from the candidate-owned checks directory to catch cwd dependency missed at project root. Handover absolute path, invocation and honest checks. Side-effect/dependency constraints also require worker source review, not inferred solely from receipt scenarios.

nodes.title: Single-file streaming CLI
nodes.text: hashslip.py parses argv before reading stdin; argparse with allow_abbrev=False; --label and --help only. Read sys.stdin.buffer in fixed-size chunks through EOF, increment byte count and hashlib.sha256, json.dump receipt then newline. JSON escaping may preserve Unicode without stdout encoding dependency. No file/network APIs, local imports, or cwd assumptions. Standard library only. Owner: sequential Contracts then Build workers on hashslip.py; exclusions: all features outside PRODUCT-BRIEF.md. Acceptance: controller S1-S10 plus candidate source review of no side effects/dependencies. Do not author extra tests or modify PRODUCT-BRIEF.md.

nodes.text: Create minimal runnable hashslip.py CLI contract stub for controller RED scenarios; owned file only, preserve source brief.

nodes.text: Implement complete HashSlip per R1-R4 and G1; validate via controller scenarios, preserve brief. Review exact candidate for stdlib-only/no runtime files/no network; report honest results.
